This marks the debut of an image generation model from Meta's Superintelligence Labs division.
The feature is expanding its reach to Facebook and Messenger soon, indicating broad platform integration.

stories.title: Facing US export controls, China's DeepSeek plans to make its own chips
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: China's DeepSeek is planning to develop its own semiconductor chips.
This initiative is a direct response to US export controls impacting access to key hardware like Nvidia GPUs.
The goal is to significantly reduce China's reliance on foreign technology providers, including Nvidia and Huawei.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when integrated with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
This represents a significant step toward faster, on-device AI inference on Apple hardware.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data and processing remain on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is the simplified setup, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in real-world robotics: the fragility of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the VLA policy self-determines camera pose (calibration-free) instead of relying on explicit extrinsic parameters.
Enhances the practical deployability and robustness of VLA systems for real-world robotic applications.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new scaling axis for improving Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities, alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of LLM solutions.
The framework provides fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
stories.author: Cong Wei
bullet_points: Addresses the 'world-knowledge bottleneck' in visual AI generators, where models confidently hallucinate outside their training data.
Introduces SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench, new benchmarks designed to test generative models against unbounded, long-tailed, and evolving user requests.
Focuses on evolving the knowledge boundary of agents by moving beyond what is explicitly taught during training.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the model learns to be view-robust without requiring explicit camera extrinsic parameters.
Significantly improves the deployability and robustness of robotic systems in dynamic, real-world environments.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new scaling axis for improving Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities, alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of solutions in agentic tasks.
The framework provides fine-grained feedback without necessitating additional model training, offering a novel approach to LLM evaluation.

stories.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Yuxiao Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the critical limitation of finite context windows in long-horizon, agentic LLMs.
Introduces CompactionRL, a novel reinforcement learning strategy to manage extended interaction trajectories.
Proposes using context compaction to summarize past states, allowing agents to operate beyond standard context limits.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new, critical scaling axis for Large Language Models (LLMs), alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a novel, general-purpose framework for determining the correctness of LLM outputs.
The framework provides fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: Every new car sold in the European Union must include a driver monitoring camera
stories.author: nickslaughter02
bullet_points: New EU regulation mandates driver monitoring cameras in all newly sold vehicles.
This represents a significant regulatory push toward in-car safety and driver attentiveness.
It signals a growing integration of surveillance/AI monitoring into consumer automotive technology.

stories.title: The best AI models cite retracted papers, and they cannot know it
stories.author: mikeeus
bullet_points: Frontier AI models are confidently citing scientific papers that have since been retracted.
The models are unaware of these retractions, demonstrating a knowledge gap related to post-training data updates.
The proposed solution requires external registry lookups, indicating a fundamental limitation in current LLM architectures.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Meta’s glasses will turn off the camera if you tamper with the privacy light
stories.author: Victoria Song
bullet_points: Meta is updating its smart glasses to include a security feature.
The camera will automatically disable if the privacy LED light is tampered with or destroyed.
This measure is specifically designed to counter unauthorized modifications by 'modders'.

stories.title: Netflix is about to host videos from BuzzFeed, Condé Nast, and other publishers
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Netflix is expanding its content library to include video from major digital publishers like BuzzFeed and Condé Nast.
The integration features a mix of previously published licensed content and new, ongoing series.
The partnership aims to bring established digital media brands' content directly into the Netflix streaming ecosystem.

stories.title: Anthropic is launching Claude Cowork on mobile and web
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Anthropic is expanding access to its Claude Cowork AI platform to mobile and web interfaces.
Initial rollout of the new access is restricted to Claude Max subscribers.
General availability for other Claude plan users is scheduled for future weeks.

stories.title: Doom developer id reportedly cut in half as part of Xbox layoffs
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: id Software, a developer of Doom, has reportedly undergone significant layoffs.
The layoffs are linked to the broader mass layoffs affecting Xbox.
Reports suggest around 50% of id Software's staff were cut, impacting departments like QA.

stories.title: Data centers’ energy demand threatens Trump’s “Made in America” plan
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The growing energy consumption of data centers is creating significant strain on electricity supply.
This energy demand is directly impacting electricity costs, particularly in the Rust Belt region.
The rising energy costs pose a threat to the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of Trump's 'Made in America' manufacturing initiatives.

stories.title: SCOTUS lets Texas enforce app store law that Big Tech calls "censorship regime"
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The 5th Circuit Court upheld Texas's law concerning app store age restrictions.
The ruling remains in place despite ongoing legal challenges from Big Tech.
The dispute highlights ongoing regulatory tension between state-level control and major tech platforms.

stories.title: Bethesda, id Software reportedly hit hard by Microsoft layoffs
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Bethesda and id Software are reportedly experiencing significant layoffs.
Some affected teams have seen reductions of up to 50% or more.
The layoffs are attributed to broader reductions within Microsoft's structure.

stories.title: This race car is made from plant fibers, volcanoes, ... and seawater?
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: A new race car, the T70S, is being constructed using unconventional, sustainable materials.
The vehicle incorporates materials derived from plant fibers, volcanic elements, and seawater.
The T70S is designed with dual functionality, suitable for both racing competitions and road use.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method to improve a powerful target model using knowledge learned from a smaller, cheaper model.
Focuses on making post-training fine-tuning more scalable and efficient as models continue to grow in size.

stories.title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
stories.author: Tai Wang
bullet_points: Cortex is a new framework designed to improve embodied AI agents for long-horizon manipulation tasks.
It addresses limitations in current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, which struggle due to their Markovian reliance on immediate observations.
The framework features a bidirectional alignment and a customized planning interface to bridge the gap between high-level planning and low-level execution.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: Introduces SPEARBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by recognizing that conversational quality depends on complex factors like timing, prosody, and interpersonal stance, not just accuracy.
Focuses on the practical application of S2S models for direct spoken query answering, pushing the boundaries of conversational AI.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a specific technical flaw in modern autoregressive ASR systems: timestamp drift during long non-speech spans.
Proposes a solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct timestamp drift without degrading transcription quality.
Validates the issue and solution across 15 different timestamp-producing ASR models using custom benchmarks.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method to improve a powerful target model using knowledge learned from a smaller, cheaper model.
Aims to make post-training refinement techniques more scalable as language models continue to grow in size.

stories.title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
stories.author: Vincenzo Piuri
bullet_points: Proposes a deep learning framework for Real-Bogus classification in transient surveys without relying on costly human labels.
The model is designed to be robust against strong class contamination and utilizes injected transients and bogus-dominated data for training.
A key feature is the provision of calibrated uncertainty quantification, enhancing the reliability of automated discovery pipelines.

stories.title: TabPack: Efficient Hyperparameter Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning
stories.author: Artem Babenko
bullet_points: Introduces TabPack, a new efficient ensemble method for deep learning on tabular data.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods where all constituent MLPs share the same hyperparameters, requiring extensive tuning.
Claims TabPack offers strong out-of-the-box performance with reduced dependence on traditional hyperparameter tuning.

stories.title: Fitted Occupancy-Ratio Evaluation without Bellman Completeness
stories.author: Nathan Kallus
bullet_points: Introduces Fitted Occupancy-Ratio Evaluation (FORE) as a new method for off-policy evaluation in reinforcement learning.
FORE bypasses the need for Bellman completeness, addressing limitations in existing primal-dual and minimax estimation methods.
The method characterizes the discounted occupancy ratio using an adjoint Bellman recursion, solving a single-level density-ratio objective iteratively.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The paper introduces a causal audit method to test if neuron attribution scores truly reflect causal importance in language models.
The research uses one-shot neuron-row zeroing to compare attribution methods against activation and magnitude-based baselines.
Findings suggest that attribution methods significantly outperform simpler baselines in identifying dispensable neuron rows for model pruning and interpretability.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: training RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: Introduces SPEARBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by focusing on conversational nuances like timing, prosody, turn-taking, and interpersonal stance.
Aims to improve the perceived quality of systems that directly respond to spoken queries with synthetic speech.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in modern ASR systems: timestamp drift occurring during long non-speech audio spans.
Proposes a novel solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct timestamp drift without degrading transcription quality.
The research evaluates this problem and solution across 15 different timestamp-producing ASR models using custom benchmarks.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between attribution scores (which identify important neurons) and true causal importance in language models.
The study employs paired audits using one-shot neuron-row zeroing to causally test the effectiveness of neuron selectors.
Attribution methods are shown to significantly outperform simpler activation and magnitude-based baselines in identifying dispensable rows.

stories.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models
stories.author: Qi Long
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM watermarking: the inability to selectively disclose embedded signals.
Existing watermarking methods (zero-bit and multi-bit) are used to verify synthetic text or embed metadata into LLM output.
The proposed work aims to enable granular control over watermark verification, preventing unnecessary information exposure.

stories.title: How Much is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
stories.author: Adam Oberman
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) maintain an internal estimate of their remaining output length.
The study uses linear probes on frozen hidden states of 7-8B open-weight models across various completion datasets.
Findings suggest that LLM responses exhibit predictable length structures (e.g., step-by-step solutions, retrievals) that may correlate with internal length tracking.

stories.title: The State of Agentic AI Standards in 2026: MCP, A2A, WebMCP, OSI, and the Protocol Stack Taking Shape
stories.author: alexmercedcoder
bullet_points: The article discusses the evolving state of Agentic AI standards, projecting into 2026.
It highlights the current fragmentation of AI agents, moving from demos (2023) to incompatible frameworks (2025).
Key standards being discussed include MCP, A2A, WebMCP, and OSI protocols for agent communication.
